# Compost

A hot pile needs roughly 30 parts carbon ("browns": dry leaves, cardboard,
straw) to 1 part nitrogen ("greens": vegetable scraps, grass clippings, coffee
grounds). Turn it every week and keep it as damp as a wrung-out sponge.

## What stays out

- Diseased plants such as tomato vines with blight; bag them instead.
- Meat, dairy and oily food, which attract rats.
- Weeds that have gone to seed.

## Timing

A well-managed hot pile is ready in about three months; a cold pile takes a
year. Finished compost smells like a forest floor.
